defs: Very good and surprising
So great that you say wow
Wonderful and hard to believe
exs: Wow, your drawing is amazing!
The magic show at school was amazing.
My dog can open the door. It is amazing!

defs: Finding something funny and smiling
Happy because something is funny
Smiling at a funny thing
exs: Dad was amused by the dog's funny dance.
The teacher looked amused when the class laughed.
She felt amused by her little brother's joke.

defs: Warm, soft and nice to stay in
Comfortable and warm
Soft and warm, like a good bed
exs: My bed is warm and cozy.
We drank hot milk in the cozy room.
The cat sleeps in a cozy box.

defs: Soft and light, like a cloud
Covered with soft hair
Soft and round, with lots of hair
exs: The white rabbit has fluffy ears.
I like my fluffy new pillow.
The baby chicken is small and fluffy.

defs: Look closely to learn about something
Check something to find out what it is
Look at something carefully to know more
exs: The cat came to investigate the new box.
Let's investigate the strange noise in the kitchen.
The boy went to investigate the big bag.

defs: Unhappy because someone gets more love
Sad because another person has something you want
Not happy when a friend gets your toy
exs: Tom was jealous of his sister's new bike.
The dog is jealous when I pet the cat.
She felt jealous when Mom hugged the baby.

defs: Look for something you cannot find
Try to find something
Look everywhere for a lost thing
exs: I search for my shoes every morning.
We search the house for the lost cat.
Let's search the bag for my pen.

defs: A little bit
Only a small amount
Not very much
exs: The soup is slightly hot.
He was slightly late for school.
My new shoes are slightly big.

defs: Said something funny to a friend
Joked in a playful way
Played a joke with words
exs: My brother teased me about my big hat.
Dad teased Mom about her funny song.
The kids teased the teacher in a kind way.

defs: Soft cloths for drying your body
Cloths you use after a bath
Cloths that dry water on you
exs: Please bring two towels to the pool.
The towels are in the bathroom.
I dry my hands with clean towels.

defs: Feeling scared about something
Not brave when you see something
Scared when you see something
exs: Many children are afraid of dark rooms.
My little sister is afraid of big dogs.
Are you afraid of snakes at the zoo?

defs: Say yes so someone can do it
Let someone do something
Say that it is okay to do
exs: Mom does not allow us to eat in bed.
The school will allow dogs on Friday.
Do your parents allow you to have a pet?

defs: Choose what to do after thinking
Pick one thing to do
Make up your mind
exs: I will decide what to eat for lunch.
We must decide which game to play.
She can't decide which red dress to buy.

defs: The way something moves or goes
Where something is going, like north or left
The way you turn or walk
exs: The bus went in the wrong direction.
Which direction is the school from here?
The birds flew in one direction.

defs: Dressed up so no one knows who the person really is.
Changed to look like something else
Covered so people can't see what it is
exs: The disguised girl looked like a cat.
A disguised dog came to the party.
The boy was disguised as a big bear.

defs: Very scared
Feeling a lot of fear
Afraid because of something bad
exs: The little boy was frightened by the thunder.
I felt frightened in the dark room.
The frightened cat ran under the bed.

defs: Covered with soft hair
Having soft hair like a cat
With thick soft hair on the body
exs: My cat is soft and furry.
I want a furry puppy.
The furry bear sleeps all winter.

defs: A thin book with pictures and stories
Something you read with news and photos
A paper book that comes out every month
exs: Dad reads a magazine on the sofa.
This magazine has many pictures of animals.
I found a funny story in the magazine.

defs: In a happy way about what you did
With a big smile about your work
Feeling very good about yourself
exs: She proudly showed us her drawing.
He proudly held up his prize.
The boy proudly said, "I did it myself!"

defs: Having long, messy hair
With long hair going everywhere
Covered with long rough hair
exs: The shaggy dog needs a bath.
He wore a shaggy hat in winter.
My uncle has long, shaggy hair.

defs: Very fast and not expected
All at once
In a quick way with no warning
exs: Suddenly, the lights went out.
The dog suddenly jumped off the bed.
It was sunny, but suddenly it rained.

defs: A place with walls and a roof
A big place like a school or a house
A tall or big place where people go in
exs: Our school building is very big.
The tall building has twenty floors.
We walked into the building together.

defs: A small room for keeping things
A place to keep clothes or tools
A small space with a door for things
exs: Mom put my coat in the closet.
The broom is in the closet.
The cat hid in the closet.

defs: A little afraid and not calm
Worried about something new
Not relaxed, with a fast heart
exs: I feel nervous on the first day of school.
She was nervous before the big test.
He felt nervous about the new class.

defs: The head teacher of a school
The boss of all teachers at school
The person who runs the school
exs: The principal spoke to all the students.
Our principal is kind and tall.
The principal visited our classroom today.

defs: An old piece of cloth
A cloth for cleaning
A piece of old cloth for wiping
exs: Dad used a rag to clean the car.
Please wipe the table with a rag.
I put an old rag over the box.

defs: Put your hand up high
Lift something up
Move something to a higher place
exs: Please raise your hand if you know.
I can raise my arms over my head.
Raise the flag in the morning.

defs: Looking at someone for a long time
Looking hard without moving the eyes
Looking at something and not stopping
exs: The baby is staring at the big dog.
Why are you staring at my hat?
The boy was staring at the cake.

defs: Say an idea for others to think about
Give an idea about what to do
Tell someone a good idea
exs: I suggest we play soccer after school.
Can you suggest a good book for me?
Mom will suggest a place for lunch.

defs: Things you need to do a job
Things kept for use, like soap and paper
Tools and things for school or work
exs: We bought school supplies for the new year.
The cleaning supplies are under the sink.
Bring your art supplies to class.
